condition: Common femoral artery aneurysm mimicking a groin hernia
summary: 74-year-old male ex-smoker with a known 4.6 cm AAA under surveillance and a pulsatile, expansile right groin swelling below the inguinal ligament. Needs duplex/CT angiography before anyone puts a needle or a knife in it; no hernia repair.

inputs.hpi: Painless right groin lump noticed 3 months ago, feels like it "throbs". Known abdominal aortic aneurysm 4.6 cm on surveillance. Ex-smoker 50 pack-years. No leg pain at rest, walks 200 yards before calf pain.

exam.abdomen: Expansile pulsatile epigastric mass. Right groin: 4 cm pulsatile, expansile swelling below the inguinal ligament over the femoral artery, with a bruit; not reducible, no cough impulse. Popliteal pulses prominent bilaterally. Foot pulses weak.

imaging.name: USS abdominal aorta (surveillance, 6 months ago)
imaging.result: Infrarenal AAA, maximum AP diameter 4.6 cm.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Right common femoral artery aneurysm (with known AAA)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Pulsatile expansile right groin mass with bruit in a patient with AAA: common femoral artery aneurysm, not a hernia. Arterial duplex / CT angiography and vascular surgery referral. Do not aspirate or explore as a hernia.

mustNotMiss.note: Pulsatile expansile groin mass with AAA: femoral aneurysm must be on the differential.

mustExclude.note: A hernia operative plan on a femoral aneurysm is dangerous.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: No vascular referral in any output (the inguinal_hernia panel is shown instead).

guideline.name: ESVS 2024 clinical practice guidelines — abdominal aorto-iliac artery aneurysms
guideline.section: Associated peripheral (femoral / popliteal) aneurysms in patients with AAA; duplex ultrasound assessment
guideline.citation: Wanhainen A, Van Herzeele I, Bastos Goncalves F, et al. European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms. Eur J Vasc Endovasc Surg. 2024;67:192–331.

guideline.name: HerniaSurge — International guidelines for groin hernia management
guideline.section: Diagnosis (clinical examination, ultrasound for uncertain swellings); watchful waiting in minimally symptomatic men; mesh repair (Lichtenstein, TEP/TAPP); groin hernia in women; femoral hernia; emergency repair
guideline.citation: HerniaSurge Group. International guidelines for groin hernia management. Hernia. 2018;22:1–165.

rationale: Groin mimic with a catastrophic failure mode (exploring or aspirating an aneurysm as a hernia). The "pulsatile mass" chip exists on web; the CC template says hernia.
